additional_wording.c12-mom-standing-wave-fit: In the circular standing-wave model, a proposed orbit has a circumference equal to (a) three electron wavelengths or (b) three and a half electron wavelengths. Which satisfies the condition for an allowed orbit? Explain how the wave matches up after one complete circuit.
additional_wording.c12-mom-probability-cloud: Bohr’s model describes an electron following a definite circular orbit. The fuller quantum description uses a probability cloud. (a) What does that cloud represent? (b) If an electron’s position is measured once, is it detected at one location or spread throughout the cloud? Explain.

answers.standing_wave_fit: Three wavelengths matches phase after a circuit; three and a half gives opposite phase and fails the periodic matching condition. This is the section’s illustrative circular-wave model, not a literal modern electron trajectory.
answers.probability_cloud: Distribution of probabilities for position detections, not a spread-out single detector event. One position measurement yields one location.

bohr_question_revised: Classical circular orbit plus quantized angular momentum only; probability-cloud comparison is now in 12.8.
